subject: Confirming ClearPath data constraints and training prohibition
messages:
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: anna@clearpath.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Post-demo recap: data handling constraints & next steps

Hi Anna — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move the procurement items forward: 

Key commitments you asked for (confirmed during call):
- No training on customer content: Redwood will not use ClearPath customer data to update or fine-tune any public or private models.
- Data residency: production inference and logs must reside in EU (prefer eu-west-1 / Ireland).
- Log retention: application and inference logs kept for 30 days, then deleted.
- PII handling: sensitive fields should be redacted or tokenized prior to storage; hashed identifiers are acceptable for dedup/analytics.
- Encryption & access: data encrypted at rest and in transit; KMS keys controlled by Redwood with optional CMK if required.

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (attestation summary) — attached for your security team.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We’ll draft a DPA reflecting the no-training clause and 30-day retention window (Marissa will own).
2) Neha will collect the SOC2 evidence and a short ops runbook describing how logs are purged.
3) I’ll follow up with a DocuSign link for the DPA and a short SOW/ops appendix for your procurement review.

Can you confirm the above captures your requirements and whether the 30-day window is firm? If yes, we’ll lock the DPA language and circulate for signature.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Anna Li <anna@clearpath.io>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: devops@clearpath.io
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 10:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: data handling constraints & next steps

Rafael — thanks for the crisp recap. That matches what we discussed. A few clarifications/additions from our side: 

- Training: we require an explicit contractual prohibition on any use of our customer content for model training or evaluation outside of the dedicated inference flow. This includes not using logs for offline model improvement.
- Residency: EU residency is required for both inference and any persisted logs. Ireland is preferred but we can accept any EU region.
- Retention: 30 days is our standard — firm. We also need a delete confirmation workflow (audit log entry) when records are purged.
- PII: we want guidance on recommended redaction patterns (PII field list). We'll work with your security team to validate approach; hashed identifiers are acceptable but must be one-way.
- Third-party attestations: please include the SOC2 Type II report or attest letter; the summary PDF is a good start but our InfoSec may ask for the attestation.

We’re ready to move quickly once the DPA has the no-training clause and the delete-audit workflow is described. Please send the DPA and any evidence you have.

Thanks — Anna Li
Head of Engineering, ClearPath Logistics
anna@clearpath.io

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: anna@clearpath.io, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 12:30:00 +01:00
Subject: DPA draft and ops checklist (next steps)

Anna / team — looping in legal/ops items and attaching an early DPA draft for review (DPA_draft_ClearPath.docx). High level:

What we’ll include in draft: 
- Explicit "no training on customer data" clause (applies to production and logs).
- 30-day retention requirement with a documented deletion schedule and audit trail for deletions.
- EU residency clause pinning region to customer-requested EU region.
- PII controls section with recommended redaction patterns and a short appendix to describe hashing vs. tokenization.

Operational items (Neha to own):
- Provide SOC2 Type II attestation and a one-page ops runbook describing log purging and proof-of-deletion (ETA EOD Tue).
- Provide a snippet of the retention automation (how retention TTLs are applied) and the audit log schema.

Proposed timeline: 
- Today: send DPA draft (attached) + SOC2 summary.
- Tue 17 Jul: Neha to deliver ops runbook and deletion proof pattern.
- Thu 19 Jul: 30-min legal review call to iterate DPA language (if needed).
- Mon 23 Jul: target signature via DocuSign.

If that works for you we’ll set the DocuSign envelope after the Thu call. Rafael — I’ll make small edits to the DPA to call out the audit proof artifact you mentioned.

Best — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: DPA_draft_ClearPath.docx
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: anna@clearpath.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 15:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Confirming ClearPath data constraints and training prohibition — DocuSign to follow

Anna — thanks for the confirmation. Quick public summary to lock expectations before we generate the DocuSign envelope: 

Agreed items (to be codified in DPA/SOW):
- No-model-training: Redwood will not use ClearPath customer data or logs to train or improve models outside of explicitly permitted, customer-authorized processes.
- EU residency: inference endpoints and any persisted logs will reside in EU region (default: eu-west-1).
- Log retention: 30-day retention window, automatic purge thereafter; deletion events recorded in an audit trail.
- PII: redaction recommended; one-way hashing allowed for identifiers.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II attestation and a one-page deletion/runbook will be attached to the DPA.

DocuSign link (will be live after our legal review): https://www.docusign.com/clearpath/CP-2028-045

Please reply with any last edits — if none, we’ll plan the Thu legal slot Marissa proposed and aim to send the DocuSign envelope Mon.
